NEW DELHI: With obesity, particularly among children, turning out to be a major health concern and number of overweight school-going kids and adolescents increasing from 2% to 10% between 2000 and 2022, Supreme Court has indicated that the health of people cannot be compromised and sent an ultimatum to Centre to implement its order for putting front-of-pack warning labels on junk food.“If the Union does it on its own, well and good, otherwise we shall proceed to pass further directions ...We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says it is not possible to match with international standards, more particularly, developed countries. Should India remain as an underdeveloped country? That’s the question we are putting forward for the Union to consider,” a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said in its order, as it linked the issue of food safety to right of life guaranteed under Article 21.The order, in response to a PIL filed by NGO ‘3S and Our HEALTH Society’ which moved SC through advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi, comes as govt has seemed reluctant to implement front-of-pack warning labels on junk food. SC said food with high salt, sugar, saturated fat and calories could lead to health risks and clearer nutrition information must be displayed to help to make healthier choices. As per Economic Survey 2025-26, India’s ultra-processed food market increased by more than 150% between 2009 and 2023, while obesity reportedly doubling.
Article Summary: Number of overweight school-going kids and adolescents increased from 2% to 10% between 2000 and 2022. SC said food with high salt, sugar, saturated fat and calories could lead to health risks. India’s ultra-processed food market increased by more than 150% between 2009 and 2023, while obesity reportedly doubling.

Article Title: How Naomi Osaka transformed her tennis success into a $120 multimillion-dollar business empire
Article Text:
Naomi Osaka (Getty Images)

Naomi Osaka net worth and tennis earnings

Naomi Osaka endorsements and business ventures

Naomi Osaka’s success cannot be measured by trophies alone. The four-time Grand Slam champion has turned her tennis fame into a much broader business empire, with major deals in fashion, sportswear and luxury goods alongside investments in companies she helped build. Her financial story shows how modern athletes can create wealth long after the applause from the court fades.Estimates place Naomi Osaka’s net worth between $45 million and $60 million, while broader assessments of her brand and business interests have put her overall economic value closer to $120 million. Those figures vary because private investments, equity holdings and future business potential are difficult to value precisely.What is clearer is where much of her wealth comes from.Osaka has earned more than $25 million in career prize money on the WTA Tour. Her four Grand Slam singles victories played a major role in building those earnings, with each major title bringing significant prize money and greater global exposure.Yet tournament checks tell only part of the story.Osaka became one of tennis’ most marketable stars at a remarkably young age.Her appeal stretches across sport, fashion and popular culture, allowing her to work with companies that want to reach audiences far beyond traditional tennis fans.That commercial reach has become a major part of her financial success.Major brand partnerships have helped Osaka build an income stream that does not depend on how she performs in a particular tournament.Nike became one of her most prominent partners after the two entered a long-term apparel agreement in 2019. Her portfolio also expanded into luxury fashion and watches, including partnerships with Louis Vuitton and TAG Heuer. These relationships placed Osaka alongside some of the world's biggest names in fashion and luxury.Her business interests go further.Osaka has invested in ventures where she can hold an ownership stake rather than simply receive payment for promoting a product. That distinction can matter enormously over time. An endorsement typically provides income for a defined partnership, while equity can potentially increase in value as a company grows.One of her notable ventures is KINLÒ, a skincare brand created with the needs of melanated skin in mind. She also co-founded Hana Kuma, a media company focused on storytelling and culturally significant projects.Her interest in sports extends into representation as well. Through Evolve, Osaka has entered the sports management space, giving her a role in helping other athletes navigate their careers.The strategy creates something larger than a collection of endorsement deals. It gives Osaka exposure to several industries while allowing her to develop assets that can remain valuable beyond her playing career.That may ultimately prove to be one of the most important parts of her financial journey.Osaka's career illustrates a major shift in professional sports. Athletes are no longer limited to earning money from competition and advertisements. The most successful can become investors, founders and business owners in their own right.Her four Grand Slam titles gave Naomi Osaka a global platform. Her business decisions have helped turn that platform into something much bigger.For Osaka, the tennis court remains central to her identity, but it is no longer the only place where her career creates value.
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka has earned more than $25 million in career prize money on the WTA Tour. The four-time Grand Slam champion has turned her tennis fame into a much broader business empire. Her financial story shows how modern athletes can create wealth long after the applause from the court fades.

Article Title: Inflation data 'concerning': Fed chair Warsh signals rates may need to rise
Article Text:
US Fed chairman Kevin Warsh

Inflation remains well above Fed's target

Markets raise rate-hike expectations

Warsh avoids 'forward guidance'

Trump keeps pressure on Fed

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh has indicated that the US central bank may need to raise interest rates in the coming months if inflation does not make enough progress towards its 2% target.Speaking at the Fed’s annual conference in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday, Warsh acknowledged that recent US data showed inflation had cooled somewhat. However, he said the figures did not indicate a meaningful improvement in underlying price pressures.“They do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved. We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed,” Warsh said, adding, “Otherwise, we have work to do.”The Fed chief did not suggest a rate hike was imminent, but his comments offered a clearer indication of his concerns about inflation. They also appeared to reassure Wall Street that controlling price pressures remains a priority for the central bank.Inflation stood at 3.7% in July according to the Fed’s preferred measure, well above its 2% target. Price pressures had cooled in June and July after rising sharply in May as gas prices surged.Warsh said inflation data “are more concerning” than trends in the labour market, where unemployment remains low. He also said inflation was unlikely to return to the Fed’s target on its own.More than half of the goods and services tracked by the government recorded price increases of 3% or more over the past year. While that was down from the pandemic peak, it remained “well above” the roughly one-third that recorded such increases in the two decades before the pandemic.The speech pushed expectations for higher short-term interest rates higher in the bond market, although US stocks remained steady.The two-year Treasury yield, which closely tracks expectations for the Fed’s federal funds rate, rose from 4.22% to 4.30%.Investors now see the chances of a rate hike at the Fed’s September 15-16 meeting as roughly even, according to futures pricing tracked by CME FedWatch. Before Warsh spoke, the probability was about one-third.Longer-term Treasury yields were mostly unchanged. The 10-year and 30-year yields showed little movement, suggesting investors did not expect higher rates to remain necessary for a prolonged period to tackle inflation.Jon Faust, an economist at Johns Hopkins and former adviser to Jerome Powell, said Warsh had conveyed a tougher approach to inflation without giving the detailed policy guidance he has criticised.“He found a way to convey that if necessary he would support raising rates, which is one thing people were concerned about,” Faust said.Michael Strain, director of economic policy studies at the American Enterprise Institute, said Warsh had previously spoken toughly about inflation without raising the Fed’s key rate. He said Friday’s comments did not provide clearer guidance on the timing of a possible move.Warsh’s speech came after his July 29 press conference created uncertainty over whether his tough comments on inflation would be followed by action.The Fed’s short-term interest rate is currently about 3.6%. Warsh has said he does not want to provide “forward guidance” on whether the central bank will raise, cut or hold rates at upcoming meetings.He argues that committing to a particular policy path would limit the Fed’s flexibility. Some economists have said he could offer more insight into his views without signalling a specific future action.Warsh reiterated his scepticism towards such guidance on Friday.He also suggested that current interest rates were not restricting economic activity, pointing to strong consumer spending and robust business investment in AI equipment and infrastructure.Fed chair clarifies policy approachWarsh also sought to clear up confusion from his July 29 news conference over the inflation measure used by the Fed and its main tool for fighting price pressures.On Friday, he specified that short-term interest rates are the Fed’s “predominant tool” and said the central bank is using the same gauge it has long followed to measure inflation.Fed chairs have often used Jackson Hole speeches to discuss broad economic and monetary policy questions or signal changes in their approach. In 2022, Powell used the event to signal that the Fed would continue sharply raising rates after pandemic-era inflation reached 9.1%, warning that the measures would bring “pain” to consumers and businesses.Warsh’s approach is being closely observed as US President Donald Trump continues to call for lower interest rates. Trump has defended Warsh, whom he appointed, while criticising other Fed officials who support higher rates.Trump has also renewed efforts to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook, appointed by former President Joe Biden. Replacing Cook would allow Trump to appoint a majority of the seven-member board. The US President tried to fire her last year but was temporarily blocked by the Supreme Court.Longer-term rates have risen in recent weeks amid factors including growing US government deficits and heavy borrowing by technology firms building AI infrastructure.The 30-year Treasury yield reached a 19-year high last week, prompting US treasury secretary Scott Bessent to make an unusual effort to buy back bonds and push yields lower.Warsh replaced Powell as Fed chair in late May after his predecessor’s term ended.
Article Summary: US Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation data ‘are more concerning’ than trends in the labour market. He also said inflation was unlikely to return to the Fed’s target on its own. The speech pushed expectations for higher short-term interest rates higher in the bond market, although US stocks remained steady.

Article Title: India vs China: How their nuclear-capable missile arsenals compare
Article Text:
The Agni family of missiles are designed to carry the weight of India's strategic weapons. (Image credit: DRDO)

China Reveals Airborne Nuclear Strike System As Xi Flexes Strategic Firepower | WATCH

Indian and Chinese strategic missiles

China and India, Asia's two most powerful countries, have spent decades building ballistic missile arsenals. These ballistic missiles are strategic weapons that act as a deterrent, under the concept of Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD). This prohibitive concept states that two nuclear armed powers will not use these weapons on each other, as the use of such a weapon will ensure a retaliatory strike, thereby increasing the cost for the attacker. India and China's strategic missile arsenals now bear resemblance, but also at the same time there are differences in capability. The two countries also are also employing different philosophies for the use of these weapons, as the US Naval Institute states that China is building a significant amount of missile capability to hit US bases in the vast Pacific.While India is building its strategic missile arsenal to act as an insurance against attacks from nuclear weapons armed entities. This concept is enshrined in India's no first use policy for nuclear weapons. India depends on the Agni family of missiles for its land based nuclear deterrence, while China depends on the Dongfeng series.At the shorter end of the spectrum, China's road-mobile DF-16 offers a range between 800 and 1,000 kilometres, giving it reach over Taiwan and much of the western Pacific.India's comparable system, the Agni-I, delivers a range of 700 to 900 kilometres, and while it lacks the DF-16's higher payload capacity of up to 1,500 kilograms, it remains a reliable, road and rail-mobile system tailored specifically for shorter-range contingencies closer to India's borders.Moving up the ladder in terms of range and capability, China's DF-21, one of the People's Liberation Army's most storied missiles, offers a range of up to 2,500 kilometres and famously spawned the world's first anti-ship ballistic missile variant, the DF-21D. India's Agni-II sits in a similar bracket, with a declared range of 2,000 to 3,500 kilometres, and has long been described as central to India's deterrence posture with respect to China, despite New Delhi's insistence that its missile programme is not aimed at any single adversary.At the intermediate range, China's DF-26, capable of striking targets over 5,000 kilometres away, including American bases in Guam, sits close in class to India's Agni-III, which offers a declared range of 3,000 to 5,000 kilometres and has been noted for a circular error probable of just around 40 metres, making it among the most accurate missiles in its class. This accuracy allows India to rely on smaller-yield warheads while still achieving high lethality, a design philosophy that keeps the system relatively compact for its range class.Where the comparison becomes genuinely interesting is at the intercontinental tier. China's DF-31A, a solid-fuel ICBM, boasts a range in excess of 11,000 kilometres. India's Agni-V, its first genuine intercontinental system, offers a declared range of 7,000 to 8,000 kilometres, though some Chinese analysts have suggested its true reach may extend closer to 8,000 kilometres once payload adjustments are factored in. Both missiles share canisterised, road-mobile configurations, a design choice that improves survivability and reduces launch preparation time.At the very top sits China's DF-41, believed to carry ten to twelve MIRV warheads across a range of 12,000 to 15,000 kilometres, making it one of the longest-range missiles in the world. India's answer, the still-developing Agni-VI, is expected to offer a comparable range of as much as 10,000 kilometres, with reports suggesting it could eventually be fitted with MIRV warheads and even a submarine-launched variant, mirroring China's own efforts to build a survivable, multi-domain nuclear triad.Taken together, the comparison suggests India has broadly kept pace with China across most range categories, even as Beijing continues to hold an edge in payload flexibility, warhead multiplicity, and the sheer scale of its overall missile inventory.
Article Summary: India and China have spent decades building ballistic missile arsenals. These ballistic missiles act as a deterrent, under the concept of Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD) China is building a significant amount of missile capability to hit US bases in the vast Pacific.

Gisele Bündchen and Tom Brady built one of the most powerful celebrity fortunes of their generation, but their paths to wealth were very different. Bündchen is widely estimated to be worth around, while Brady’s current fortune is estimated by some sources at roughly. The surprising part is not that Brady became enormously wealthy. It is how consistently Bündchen’s fashion career generated money on a global scale.Gisele Bündchen entered modeling as a teenager and turned a traditional fashion career into a worldwide business. She became the world’s highest-paid model for much of the period from 2002 through 2017, according to Forbes-linked reporting.Her earnings did not depend on runway appearances alone. Major campaigns, beauty contracts, fragrances and brand partnerships helped transform her fame into long-term income. Forbes reported that Bündchen earned about $30.5 million in 2016, with deals involving brands such as Chanel and Carolina Herrera, alongside her own business ventures.Her career earnings were remarkable even before she stepped away from regular runway work. Forbes estimated in 2014 that she had earned $386 million from modeling since 2001.That helps explain the wealth gap. Bündchen was not simply being paid to wear clothes.She became the face of international brands and developed businesses connected to her name.Her income also continued beyond modeling through products, endorsements and investments. That broader strategy allowed her to turn a highly visible career into lasting wealth.Brady’s fortune was built differently. His biggest financial engine was his 23-year NFL career, during which he collected substantial playing salaries and bonuses. Forbes reported that he earned about $333 million from playing contracts, with another $200 million coming from endorsements and other ventures.But Brady has never relied solely on football. His business portfolio includes the TB12 brand, the BRADY clothing line, production ventures and Autograph. He has also invested in professional sports teams, including the Las Vegas Raiders and other franchises.His post-NFL career added another major income stream. Brady signed a reportedto become its lead NFL analyst.So, how is Gisele Bündchen richer than Tom Brady?The answer is timing, scale and the economics of their industries. Bündchen reached the top of a global fashion market for years, earning enormous endorsement income while building businesses of her own. Brady earned extraordinary sums from football, but his biggest playing contracts arrived within a sport where even the greatest players had different salary structures.Their fortunes also show why celebrity wealth cannot be judged simply by fame. Brady may have seven Super Bowl rings, but Bündchen built a global commercial brand that kept generating value far beyond the runway.
Article Summary: Gisele Bündchen entered modeling as a teenager and turned a traditional fashion career into a worldwide business. Brady’s biggest financial engine was his 23-year NFL career, during which he collected substantial playing salaries and bonuses. Brady earned extraordinary sums from football but his biggest playing contracts arrived within a sport where even the greatest players had different salary structures.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay flags off 250 new buses, including 130 electric buses
Article Text:
Chief Minister S. Joseph Vijay flags off new buses at St George Fort in Chennai on Tuesday.

(With Agency Inputs)





CHENNAI: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday inaugurated new bus services operated by the Metropolitan Transport Corporation (MTC) and Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporations at the Secretariat.He flagged off 130 low-floor electric buses worth Rs 234.5 crore and 120 other buses worth Rs 55.8 crore for public use.The 130 EV buses are from Switch Mobility, a subsidiary of Ashok Leyland and are part of Tamil Nadu’s broader green mobility programme.The CM boarded one of the buses and inspected its amenities.Earlier on Monday, CM Vijay announced the expansion of the fare-free bus travel scheme for women, making services such as deluxe and express buses free for beneficiaries.Making several announcements in the Assembly, Vijay, fulfilling TVK's key electoral assurances, announced three free cooking gas cylinders and also declared that the Parandur greenfield airport project will be shelved.The project had been strongly opposed by farmers who did not wish to part with their farm lands."There will be no riders like income ceiling or number of trips for women to avail fare-free bus travel - Vettri Payanam," Vijay said, making a statement under Rule 110.Women can also travel free of charge on Express, LSS and Deluxe government buses operating in metropolitan and urban areas, as well as on regular fare buses in suburban (Mofussil) and hilly areas.The scheme will be rolled out on October 2, coinciding with Gandhi Jayanthi. Vijay said the move will entail an additional expenditure of Rs 6,000 crore per annum for the state government.On the Annapoorani Super Six scheme, a major welfare promise made by Vijay in the run-up to the April Assembly election, assuring six free LPG cylinders to every eligible family in Tamil Nadu every year to reduce household living expenses, the Chief Minister said three free cooking gas cylinders will initially be provided, with the amount credited directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries."This will reduce the burden of the people who have been spending extra amount to obtain the cylinders. The government has decided to provide the cost of the cooking gas cylinders. Three free LPG cylinders will be given in the first phase and the price for cylinders will be directly credited into the bank accounts of the beneficiaries," Vijay said, amidst loud thumping of tables by the Treasury.The move will benefit 1,30,16,104 families with an annual income of nearly Rs 2.5 lakh, economically backward families, small and medium farmers, differently abled people and poor families."The preparatory work has commenced and the scheme will be launched this Pongal (mid-January) 2027 festival," Vijay said and added the state government will allocate Rs 4,000 crore per annum for this initiative.
Article Summary: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday inaugurated new bus services operated by the Metropolitan Transport Corporation (MTC) and Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporations at the Secretariat. He flagged off 130 low-floor electric buses worth Rs 234.5 crore and 120 other buses worth £ 55.8 crore for public use.
